expression_comparison.chosen_because: This seat stays in USD spot. USDCAD is the defensible pair: largest verified rates gap, growth/labor split, unstretched 1y valuation versus other USD pairs, and no need for a non-USD cross.
expression_comparison.cross_attack: AUDNZD at 1.2388 is 99.8th 1y / 99.96th 5y with z_5y 2.96. That stretch is a cross-merchant toy, not a USD view. It layers RBA housing stress, an India-NZ trade tail, and unavailable NZ rates on top of two commodity currencies. It does not own the Fed hike, the US 2Y 4.67% print, or the CA-US 139bp 2Y gap. Second-order risk without the USD benchmark.

usd_pair_comparison.assessment: Preferred. USD leg: delivered hike, inflation/labor hot, 2Y 4.67%. CAD leg: 2Y 3.35%, labor 38 vs US 75, consumer 45 vs US 74, core near 2%. Spot 1y 70.8th / 5y 86.2nd is rich-ish but not 99th; 3m still -1.17% so residual catch-up remains. Positive carry. Energy is the CAD-specific risk, not a reason to leave USD.

Inferior USD expression. ECB also hiked 25bp on energy inflation, so both legs tightened. EURUSD 1.1481 is already 13.3rd 1y percentile; the 5d -1.16% is largely spent. Less residual relative-policy gap than USDCAD.

Fights carry. AU-US 2Y still +40.5bp and AU 10Y 5.202% versus US 10Y 4.94% as of 9 Sep (AU snapshot 8 days stale). AU inflation gauge 82 exceeds US 72. Housing is biting, but short AUDUSD is not a clean USD-policy trade.
NZD already cheap (1y 21.2nd / 5y 11.5th) and NZ official rates are unavailable. India trade deal is a NZD-positive idiosyncratic. Do not force a USD/NZD view on a missing rates book.
No Japan policy in packet. 20d RV 9.74, 1m -2.13% / 3m -3.76% already JPY-strong. High second-order vol without a verified BoJ leg.
1y percentile 99.8 / z_1y 2.28. Statistical stretch without a Swiss policy item. Bad USD entry.

remit: express macro views through USD spot whenever a defensible USD pair exists
stance_summary: The cleanest expression of post-hike USD policy exceptionalism is long USDCAD spot, not a non-USD cross: the CAD leg is the weak rates/labor offset, while EUR, JPY, AUD and NZD either already repriced, fight carry, or add second-order risk.
thesis: USD is the benchmark; express the post-FOMC inflation/policy premium in a USD pair, not a cross.
CAD is the weaker offsetting leg on verified rates, labor and core inflation, so USDCAD owns the discrepancy.
AUDNZD/EUR crosses add unnecessary second-order risk and do not isolate the Fed premium.

Oil remaining contained after the Saudi-Oman workaround, denying CAD a terms-of-trade rescue.

trade.invalidation: Falsify if the CAD leg re-prices as a tighter policy peer: BoC communication or data showing energy pass-through into core, a sustained narrowing of the CA-US 2Y gap from the bottom-decile print, or a renewed oil-supply shock that re-bids CAD on terms of trade. Do not invent a spot stop; ECB references are not executable.
trade.mispricing: CA-US 2Y is -139bp (1y percentile 4.8, 5y percentile 4.7) as of 2026-09-16, yet ECB-reference USDCAD is only 70.8th 1y / 86.2nd 5y and is still -1.17% over 3m. The front-end gap widened as US 2Y rose 48bp over 1m versus CA 2Y +38bp, while USDCAD is only +0.89% over 1m. FX has not fully paid the verified policy/rates discrepancy. USDCHF and USDSEK at the 99.8th 1y percentile are the stretched USD pairs; USDCAD is not.
principal_risks: BoC energy pass-through warning becomes a hike path, compressing CA-US yields and bidding CAD.
Oil spike or weaker energy shock absorbers reverse the CAD terms-of-trade leg.
Hike was >90% priced; USD premium was partly spent in the 5d USDCAD +1.30% bounce.
Temperature gauges are dashboard-retained/stale; positioning is empty; ECB FX is a reference, not a tradable print.
trade.thesis: Own USD versus CAD in spot. The USD leg is a delivered 25bp hike into still-hot inflation, labor and front-end yields; the CAD leg is a 139bp 2Y cheapness versus the US, weak labor/consumer gauges, and headline 3% with core near 2%. That relative-policy gap is a USD-pair problem. AUDNZD, EURGBP or other crosses add RBA-housing, missing-NZ-rates, or ECB-energy second-order risk without owning the Fed premium.
why_now: FOMC delivered +25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep after >90% hike pricing; residual USD edge is path/premium versus CAD, not the announcement surprise.
US 2Y 4.67% (17 Sep) versus CA 2Y 3.35% (16 Sep) leaves long USDCAD with verified positive carry while the 3m USDCAD print is still negative.
Saudi ship-to-ship workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail that would have bid CAD; that is a now-dated CAD support, not a reason to express the view in a commodity cross.
US August CPI, accelerating PPI, nonfuel import prices and rising Michigan inflation expectations keep the Fed tightening bias live against CA core near 2%.

what_changes_my_mind: BoC tightens or core inflation re-accelerates through energy, collapsing CA-US 2s.
US inflation/labor gauges roll over and US 2Y gives back the 1m +48bp move.
Oil re-spikes enough that CAD terms of trade dominate the rates gap.
A cleaner USD pair appears with a larger unspent rates-versus-spot discrepancy and less energy beta.
why_now: Hike is delivered; the live question is whether CAD still trades as if the 139bp 2Y gap and weak labor do not require a weaker CAD.
5d USDCAD +1.30% is catch-up, not completion, while 3m USDCAD remains -1.17%.
Oil-tail relief removes a CAD bid that would otherwise justify staying in a commodity cross.
